en.headline: New World removes Emperor Theatre relief over collapse risk, studies restoration
en.dek: The developer said the 8-metre Chan Mi Dong Zhuo artwork on the Grade 1 North Point building had structural problems and was removed with Buildings Department approval.
body: New World Development has removed the large Chan Mi Dong Zhuo relief from the front of the Grade 1 historic Emperor Theatre building in North Point after inspections found structural risks, the company said.

The 8-metre-high by 8-metre-wide relief, by Lingnan school artist Mei Yutian, depicts a scene from Romance of the Three Kingdoms and incorporates Western elements. New World, which acquired the building in 2020, said the lower central section had been converted into a ventilation opening years earlier, with severe weathering and rusted supports creating a collapse risk.

The company applied to the Buildings Department last year and received approval to remove it. The relief is now stored while restoration methods and feasibility are studied. Scaffolding has been taken down, leaving a plain wall. The building is expected to reopen around the middle of next year.
New World has said it is seeking experts to restore the work using available sketches. The Development Bureau had not responded to queries by press time.

zh.headline: 新世界因倒塌風險移除皇都戲院浮雕 正研究修復
zh.dek: 發展商表示北角一級歷史建築正門8米高「蟬迷董卓」浮雕有結構問題，已獲屋宇署批准移除並妥善存放。
body: 新世界發展表示，北角一級歷史建築皇都戲院大廈正門大型「蟬迷董卓」浮雕因結構風險已移除，現正研究修復方式。
這幅高8米、闊8米的浮雕由嶺南畫派畫家梅與天創作，取材《三國演義》情節並加入西方元素。新世界於2020年收購大廈後，發現浮雕中間下方早年已改為通風口，內部嚴重風化、支架生鏽，存在倒塌風險。
集團去年向屋宇署申請並獲批准移除浮雕，現已妥善存放。棚架拆除後該處現為白牆。大廈預計明年中重開。
新世界表示正物色專家，並已取得草圖，研究恢復原貌的可行性。發展局截稿前未有回覆查詢。
